$comment: WEIGHTS-001 — the manifest git DOES hold, describing the weights git does NOT.
Rule: no binary weight ever enters this repository. Binaries are immortal in git history
and cannot be removed without rewriting it, so the only safe policy is to never add one.
This file plus scripts/fetch_weights.py is what makes a fresh machine reproducible.
`kind` tells the fetcher how to provision an entry:
hf        — huggingface_hub snapshot_download at a PINNED revision (a commit sha, never a
branch: 'main' is a moving target and would silently change which weights run)
url       — direct download to `dest`, verified against `sha256`
pip-git   — installed by requirements-ml.txt; the fetcher only reports, never installs
torch-hub — pulled by torch.hub at load time into TORCH_HOME; the fetcher pre-warms it and,
where the upstream call omits trust_repo, pre-seeds the trusted_list so a fresh
box never blocks on an interactive y/N prompt
`mirror_needed: true` marks artifacts we do NOT control and cannot re-fetch if upstream
removes them. See vault/Build/Architecture Lab/Decisions/weights-storage.md for the plan.

models.name: fashion_clip
models.size_human: 581 MB (of ~1.2 GB in the repo — the rest is ONNX we never load)
models.notes: Largest HF entry. `ignore_patterns` is load-bearing, not an optimisation: the repo ships an onnx/ variant directory that this codebase never touches (fashion_clip_service uses CLIPModel/CLIPProcessor on safetensors; nothing in backend/ imports onnx). Without it a full snapshot pulls ~600 MB of dead weight AND the cache check never passes — the local cache here has 8 abandoned .incomplete ONNX blobs from exactly that. `pytorch_model.bin` is excluded for the same reason: the repo ships both formats, transformers loads safetensors, and demanding the .bin too made every run report an IncompleteSnapshotError and re-attempt a download that would never be used.

models.name: florence2_base
models.size_human: ~0.5 GB (safetensors only; the repo also ships a redundant .bin)
models.notes: The Director's local eyes: one model covering caption / detect / grounding / referring-expression segmentation. STATUS: weights provisioned, adapter DEFERRED — this checkpoint does not load under transformers 5.13. Natively it fails 'RobertaTokenizer has no attribute image_token' (the native Florence2Processor targets a converted checkpoint format this repo predates); with trust_remote_code=True it fails "'Florence2LanguageConfig' object has no attribute 'forced_bos_token_id'" (the repo's remote code was written for transformers 4.x). No native conversion exists on the hub. Activation therefore needs a decision, not a flag — see the P8-A report. `ignore_patterns` excludes pytorch_model.bin for the fashion-clip reason: the repo ships both formats and demanding the redundant one makes the snapshot permanently 'incomplete'.

models.name: grounding_dino_tiny
models.size_human: 657 MB (safetensors; the repo also ships a redundant .bin)
models.notes: Grounded-SAM's detector half: a phrase grounds to a BOX, which the already-live SAM2 refines into a mask. Chosen over Florence-2 because it loads NATIVELY on transformers 5.13 (GroundingDinoForObjectDetection, no remote code at all) — Florence-2 does not, either natively or via trust_remote_code. Apache-2.0, so unlike YOLO's AGPL it carries no distribution constraint.

models.name: clip_vit_b32
models.size_human: 577 MB (of ~1.7 GB in the repo — flax + TF duplicates we never load)
used_by: P8-C presence gate: does the detector's crop actually match the phrase?
models.notes: A GENERAL CLIP, deliberately distinct from fashion_clip: the presence gate judges arbitrary curator phrases on arbitrary images, and a fashion-tuned encoder would score a Pietà against 'the drapery' on the wrong manifold. Exists because GroundingDINO has no presence head (P8-B measured absent phrases outscoring present ones), so a second, independent opinion is what lets the detector threshold drop without letting fabrications through. WEIGHTS NOTE, inverted from every other entry here: this repo ships NO safetensors — pytorch_model.bin is the only usable weights file, and the flax/TF duplicates are 577 MB each. So `required_files` names the .bin and `ignore_patterns` drops flax/tf, the reverse of the fashion-clip case. Copying the usual pattern would have excluded the only weights and required a file that does not exist — caught by the required_files verification added in P8-A.
